paper.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

concepts.name: Constitutional AI (CAI)
concepts.summary: A two-stage method for training a harmless language model assistant using only a set of written principles rather than human harmfulness labels, combining supervised self-critique/revision with reinforcement learning from AI-generated preference labels.

locators.section: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

concepts.notes: Umbrella method comprising the SL stage (critique and revision) and the RL stage (RLAIF); replaces human harmfulness labels used in prior RLHF work.

concepts.name: Constitution (set of principles)
concepts.summary: The small set of natural-language principles/instructions that provide the sole source of human guidance for steering model critiques, revisions, and preference comparisons in CAI.

locators.section: C Constitutional Principles Used for This Research

concepts.notes: Instantiated as two separate principle lists: one for SL-CAI critiques/revisions (C.1) and one for RL-CAI comparisons (C.2).

concepts.name: Principles for SL-CAI (Appendix C.1)
concepts.summary: The specific list of 16 critique/revision instruction pairs used to steer the supervised critique-and-revision phase.

concepts.name: Principles for RL-CAI (Appendix C.2)
concepts.summary: The specific list of 16 multiple-choice comparison principles used by the feedback model to label which of two responses is more harmless.

concepts.name: Critique and Revision
concepts.summary: The supervised-stage pipeline in which a model critiques its own harmful response according to a sampled constitutional principle and then revises the response to remove the identified harm.

locators.section: 3 Constitutional AI: Critiques, Revisions, and Supervised Learning

concepts.notes: Applied repeatedly (chained) to produce a sequence of progressively less harmful revisions; feeds into SL-CAI finetuning.

concepts.name: SL-CAI (Supervised-Learning Constitutional AI model)
concepts.summary: The model produced by finetuning a pretrained LM on constitutionally revised harmlessness responses plus helpfulness samples, serving as the initial policy for the RL stage.
concepts.notes: Variants SL-CAI-n are trained on up to n revisions (n=1..4); more helpful and harmless than pretrained models but less helpful than RLHF models.

concepts.name: RL-CAI (RLAIF-trained Constitutional AI model)
concepts.summary: The final policy produced by running RL against a preference model trained partly on AI-generated harmlessness labels, starting from the SL-CAI snapshot.

locators.section: 4 Constitutional AI: Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback

concepts.notes: More harmless than RLHF and SL-CAI at comparable helpfulness; reported as virtually never evasive, reducing the evasiveness seen in prior HH RLHF.

concepts.name: RL from AI Feedback (RLAIF)
concepts.summary: A variant of RLHF in which the harmlessness preference labels used to train the reward/preference model are generated by an AI feedback model instead of human crowdworkers.

locators.section: 4 Constitutional AI: Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback

concepts.notes: Helpfulness labels remain human-sourced, so the resulting preference model is a human/AI hybrid.

concepts.name: Feedback Model
concepts.summary: An independent (typically pretrained) language model presented with a harmful prompt and a pair of responses that produces the multiple-choice harmlessness preference label used to construct the AI feedback dataset.

concepts.name: Hybrid Human/AI Preference Model
concepts.summary: A preference model trained on a mixture of human-labeled helpfulness comparisons and AI-labeled harmlessness comparisons.

concepts.name: Preference Model (PM)
concepts.summary: A model trained on comparison data to assign a scalar score to a response, used as the reward signal for RL, following the RLHF pipeline of prior work.

concepts.name: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)
concepts.summary: The established technique of training a policy with RL against a preference model fit to human comparison judgments; CAI extends and partially replaces it for harmlessness.

concepts.name: Helpful RLHF Model
concepts.summary: An RLHF policy trained using only helpfulness human-feedback comparisons, used as the harmful-response-generating starting point for the SL-CAI critique/revision pipeline.

concepts.name: HH RLHF Model
concepts.summary: An RLHF policy trained on both helpfulness and harmlessness human-feedback comparisons, used as a baseline comparison against RL-CAI throughout the paper.

concepts.name: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Prompting
concepts.summary: A prompting technique that elicits intermediate step-by-step reasoning from a language model before its final answer, used here both for SL critiques and to make the RL feedback model's harmlessness judgments more accurate and transparent.
concepts.notes: Improves preference-label accuracy substantially at scale (Figure 4) but makes soft labels overconfident, motivating label clamping.

concepts.name: "Let's think step-by-step" zero-shot CoT trigger
concepts.summary: A specific zero-shot prompt phrase from Kojima et al. (2022) appended to elicit chain-of-thought reasoning from the feedback model before it commits to a multiple-choice harmlessness judgment.

concepts.name: Multiple-Choice Comparison Format
concepts.summary: The prompt template that presents a conversation, a constitutional principle, and two candidate responses labeled (A)/(B), from which the feedback model's answer log-probabilities become the preference label.

concepts.name: Preference Label Clamping (Soft vs. Hard vs. Clamped)
concepts.summary: A technique for constructing PM training targets from feedback-model outputs, comparing raw soft (normalized log-probability) labels, hard 0/1 labels, and probabilities clamped to a fixed range (e.g. 40-60%) to counteract CoT-induced overconfidence.
concepts.notes: Clamping at 40-60% found to give the most robust RL-CAI behavior; without it, CoT-based soft labels are nearly 0 or 1 and RL-CAI learns overly extreme responses.

concepts.name: Principle Ensembling
concepts.summary: Randomly sampling a different constitutional principle for each comparison label (rather than reusing one principle for all labels) to produce more robust preference-model behavior.

concepts.name: Evasiveness
concepts.summary: A named failure mode in which a harmlessness-trained assistant gives canned refusals (e.g. "I can't answer that") to sensitive queries instead of engaging, sacrificing transparency and helpfulness for apparent safety.

locators.section: A Harmless but Non-Evasive (Still Helpful) Assistant

concepts.notes: CAI is designed specifically to reduce evasiveness relative to the prior HH RLHF model of Bai et al. (2022); RL-CAI is reported as virtually never evasive.

concepts.name: Helpfulness-Harmlessness Tension
concepts.summary: The observed tradeoff whereby increasing a model's willingness to help tends to increase its potential for harm, and increasing harmlessness training tends to make a model more evasive and less helpful.
concepts.notes: CAI aims to shift the Pareto frontier of this tradeoff rather than simply trading one for the other.

concepts.name: Goodharting (Reward Over-Optimization)
concepts.summary: A named failure mode in which over-training against the preference-model reward causes RL-CAI to become overly harsh, boilerplate, or accusatory toward harmless-seeming prompts, degrading true response quality despite improving proxy reward.
concepts.notes: Cites Gao et al. (2022) 'Scaling laws for reward model overoptimization'; observed as repetitive boilerplate like 'you are valid, valued, and cared for'.

concepts.name: Scaling Supervision
concepts.summary: An umbrella term for techniques that use AI systems to help humans supervise other AIs more efficiently, of which Constitutional AI is presented as an extreme instance.

concepts.name: Elo Score (helpfulness/harmlessness)
concepts.summary: A rating computed from crowdworker pairwise model-comparison preferences, used throughout the paper to track relative helpfulness and harmlessness of model snapshots during training.

concepts.name: Helpful, Honest, and Harmless (HHH)
concepts.summary: The three-part objective for AI assistant behavior established in prior work, which CAI aims to satisfy without human harmfulness labels.

concepts.name: HHH Evaluation Set (binary comparisons)
concepts.summary: A benchmark of binary response-comparison questions testing whether a model can identify the more helpful, honest, and harmless reply; originally 221 comparisons from Askell et al. (2021) on BIG-Bench, extended here with 217 additional harder harmlessness-focused comparisons.

locators.section: 2 Evaluating the Potential for AI Supervision of HHH
B Identifying and Classifying Harmful Conversations

concepts.name: BIG-Bench
concepts.summary: A large collaborative benchmark suite for language models that hosts the original HHH evaluation set used as a comparison baseline.

locators.section: B Identifying and Classifying Harmful Conversations

concepts.name: Model Calibration (well-calibrated multiple-choice probabilities)
concepts.summary: The property, established in prior work, that language models' probabilities on multiple-choice questions are reasonably well-calibrated, which CAI relies on to treat feedback-model output probabilities as usable soft preference labels.

concepts.name: Absolute Harmfulness Score
concepts.summary: A single-conversation harmfulness metric (0-4 scale) predicted by a model finetuned with L2 loss on crowdworker absolute-harm ratings, used as an additional evaluation signal alongside pairwise Elo comparisons.
concepts.notes: Labels originally collected in Ganguli et al. (2022); this paper trains a dedicated scorer and reports it in Figure 10.

concepts.name: Red Teaming
concepts.summary: The practice of having crowdworkers conduct adversarial conversations designed to bait a language model into harmful outputs, used as the source of harmful prompts for both SL-CAI and RL-CAI training.

concepts.name: Automated Red Teaming
concepts.summary: A related approach (Perez et al., 2022) of using language models themselves to generate red-team prompts, noted as a future direction that CAI's non-evasiveness should make easier to scale up.

locators.section: A Harmless but Non-Evasive (Still Helpful) Assistant

concepts.name: PALMS (Process for Adapting Language Models to Society)
concepts.summary: A prior values-targeted dataset of sensitive questions (Solaiman & Dennison, 2021) used here as a fixed prompt set for qualitatively comparing HH RLHF and RL-CAI responses.

concepts.name: LaMDA
concepts.summary: Google's dialogue language model (Thoppilan et al., 2022), cited as related aligned-dialogue-agent work and as a source of comparison prompts and reference responses in Appendix D.

concepts.name: InstructGPT
concepts.summary: OpenAI's instruction-tuned language model (Ouyang et al., 2022), cited as related RLHF-based alignment work and as a source of comparison prompts in Appendix D.

concepts.name: Sparrow
concepts.summary: DeepMind's dialogue agent (Glaese et al., 2022), cited as related work whose decomposition of harmlessness into targeted rules parallels this paper's use of constitutional principles.

concepts.name: Context Distillation
concepts.summary: A prior finetuning technique of distilling a lengthy prompt's behavior into model weights, used for RLHF models in earlier work but not for the RLHF models trained directly in this paper.

concepts.name: Few-shot Prompts for SL-CAI (Appendix E.1)
concepts.summary: Hand-written few-shot conversation/critique/revision examples prepended to the SL-CAI critique- and revision-generating model to prevent point-of-view confusion between critique and revision roles.

concepts.name: Chain-of-Thought Prompts for RL-CAI (Appendix E.2)
concepts.summary: Hand-written few-shot examples, each with a substitutable principle placeholder, used to prompt the feedback model to produce step-by-step reasoning before its multiple-choice harmlessness judgment.

concepts.name: Direct Revision (critique-free ablation)
concepts.summary: An ablation of the SL-CAI pipeline that skips the critique step and asks the model to generate a revision directly, compared against critiqued revisions to test whether the critique step is necessary.
concepts.notes: Critiqued revisions score higher for small models; roughly equal for large models, but critiqued revisions were used for the main results for transparency.

concepts.name: Harmful Behavior Identification/Classification Evaluations (Appendix B)
concepts.summary: Two multiple-choice evaluations built from red-teaming transcripts: identifying harmful vs. ethical assistant behavior, and classifying harmful conversations into one of nine categories, used to test whether models can replicate crowdworker harm judgments.

locators.section: B Identifying and Classifying Harmful Conversations

concepts.name: Pareto Improvement (helpfulness vs. harmlessness)
concepts.summary: The finding that Constitutional RL shifts the helpfulness-harmlessness tradeoff frontier outward rather than just moving along the standard RLHF tradeoff curve.

concepts.name: Iterated (Online) Training
concepts.summary: A training regime from prior work in which the preference model is periodically refreshed with new comparison data collected on the current policy's outputs, keeping the PM on-distribution; noted as a future direction now automatable with AI feedback.
